items.readable_text:
Content:
A triangle is a geometric shape that consists of three points connected by three line segments, as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b3dac3050cddb464a6344bda09e19797]

Content:
For this triangle,

Content:
- the line segments [MATH: \overline{AB}], [MATH: \overline{BC}] and [MATH: \overline{CA}] are the sides of the triangle,
- the points [MATH: \color{red}A], [MATH: \color{red}B] and [MATH: \color{red}C] are the vertices of the triangle,
- the angles [MATH: \angle{A}], [MATH: \angle{B}] and [MATH: \angle{C}] formed by the sides are called the interior angles of the triangle.

Content:
To denote a triangle, we use the symbol [MATH: \boldsymbol{\triangle}] and list its vertices (in any order). So, the above diagram shows us [MATH: \triangle ABC.]

Content:
It can be shown that all triangles have the following property:

Content:
> The sum of the measures of the interior angles of any triangle is always equal to [MATH: 180^\circ.]

Content:
For example, in [MATH: \triangle ABC] shown above, the interior angle theorem tells us that
[MATH: m\angle{A} + m\angle{B} + m\angle{C} = 180^\circ .]

Content:
Therefore, if we know the measures of two angles in a triangle, we can calculate the value of the other.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
A triangle is a geometric shape that consists of three points connected by three line segments, as shown below.

- the points [MATH: \color{red}A], [MATH: \color{red}B] and [MATH: \color{red}C] are the vertices of the triangle,
- the angles [MATH: \angle{A}], [MATH: \angle{B}] and [MATH: \angle{C}] formed by the sides are called the interior angles of the triangle.

Content:
To denote a triangle, we use the symbol [MATH: \boldsymbol{\triangle}] and list its vertices (in any order). So, the above diagram shows us [MATH: \triangle ABC.]

It can be shown that all triangles have the following property:

Content:

For example, in [MATH: \triangle ABC] shown above, the interior angle theorem tells us that
[MATH: m\angle{A} + m\angle{B} + m\angle{C} = 180^\circ .]

Content:
Therefore, if we know the measures of two angles in a triangle, we can calculate the value of the other.
